A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel approach for evaluating web sources that does not rely on external signals and that we show it can be used to reliably compute trustworthiness scores.
we proposed a novel way to estimate the trustworthinss of web sources by using the correctness of their factual information and that we showed that our method is effective in doing so.
we proposed a new way to evaluate the trustworthiness (or credibility) of a source based on the correctness of the facts it provides.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the trustworthiness levels we compute can be used as an additional signal for ranking search results.
it is possible to automatically estimate the trustworthness of web sources, and this can be done without relying on exogenous signals.
the trustworthiness levels computed using our method correlate with other exogenous signals, but they are more robust to changes in the hyperlink graph.
